title: Definitions Entry — The Final Part of the Cycle on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Definitions Entry — The Final Part of the Cycle on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

**The number of days the final part of the cycle runs to**, where a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan is settled, is counted to the handling date from one of three dates, according to what the plan's records show.

1. Where a payment has settled on the plan in the whole month ending on the handling date, the days run from the date of the most recent settled payment to the handling date.
2. Where no payment has settled in the whole month ending on the handling date and the plan stands past due, the days run from the payment due date printed on the most recent statement to the handling date.
3. In every other case, the days run from the closing date of the most recent statement to the handling date.

The first condition is tested first: a settled payment credited in the whole month ending on the handling date fixes the anchor on that payment's date whatever the plan's standing. The second is reached only where that month holds no settled payment and the plan stands past due.

## The three anchors, on hypothetical dates

Take a handling date of 18 September. The most recent statement closed on 2 September and printed a payment due date of 27 September; the most recent settled payment on the plan was credited on 9 September.

| What the records show | Anchor date | Days to the handling date |
|---|---|---|
| The 9 September payment settled, and it falls in the whole month ending on 18 September | 9 September | 9 |
| No payment settled in that month and the plan stands past due | 27 September, the due date printed on the most recent statement | The days from that printed due date to the handling date |
| No payment settled in that month and the plan stands active | 2 September, the closing date of the most recent statement | 16 |
